extra.message: User-controlled registration code is formatted directly into a raw SQL query using sqlalchemy.text() in validate_token(). An attacker can inject SQL payloads via the registration_code form field to read or modify the database.
The search query parameter is concatenated into a LIKE clause passed to sqlalchemy.text(). This allows authenticated users to perform SQL injection via the ?search= parameter.

render_template_string() is called with an f-string containing request.path, which is attacker-controlled. A request path such as /{{config}} or /{{7*7}} is evaluated as Jinja2, leading to server-side template injection and information disclosure.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: The preferences cookie value is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads() in before_request(). An attacker who forges or modifies the preferences cookie can execute arbitrary Python code during deserialization.

download() calls urllib.request.urlopen() with a user-supplied URL from /account/image with no allowlist, protocol restrictions, or size limits. This allows SSRF to internal services and local file reads (e.g. file:// URLs).

get_personal_notes() queries notes for the supplied user_id without verifying the requested user_id matches current_user.id. Any authenticated user can enumerate or view other users' personal notes by changing the URL path parameter.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: delete_note() fetches and deletes a note solely by note_id without checking that the note belongs to current_user or that current_user is an admin. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's note by posting to /notes/<id>/delete.

update_account() lacks the @login_required decorator, so it is reachable without authentication. Additionally, the AccountForm includes an is_admin field and update_account() copies form values directly into current_user.__dict__, allowing any authenticated user to escalate privileges to admin.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Note text is rendered with the |safe filter, disabling Jinja2 autoescaping. Because notes are stored and displayed to other users, a stored XSS payload in note.text executes in victims' browsers.
render_table() is called with safe_columns=['text'], marking note text as safe HTML. Stored note content containing JavaScript will execute when the search results are rendered.
render_table() is called with safe_columns=['text'], marking note text as safe HTML. Stored note content containing JavaScript will execute when personal notes are rendered.

current_user.profile_image is rendered inside an <object> data attribute as a data URI with a MIME type guessed from the attacker-supplied URL. A URL ending in .html causes a data:text/html URI, so stored HTML/JS in the downloaded image content executes when the navigation bar is rendered.

add_image() calls get_base64_image_blob() on a user-controlled URL without enforcing timeouts, maximum response sizes, or content-type validation. An attacker can cause denial of service by supplying a huge or slow-responding URL.

add_note() processes POST requests from a wtforms.Form subclass that does not inherit from Flask-WTF FlaskForm, so no CSRF token is generated or validated. Attackers can trick authenticated users into creating notes via CSRF. The same issue affects delete_note and other POST routes.
Flask secret_key is set to a hardcoded, static string. This allows attackers to forge session cookies and bypass authentication.
A static registration code (a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764) is hardcoded in the database seed logic. Anyone with knowledge of this backdoor code can register an account.

The SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, causing all SQL statements (including those containing user data, passwords, and tokens) to be logged to stdout. This exposes sensitive information in logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The preferences cookie is set without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes. The same insecure configuration is repeated in after_request() at lines 127-128, exposing the cookie to theft via XSS and CSRF.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
